title: intersection-observer 0.12.2: W3C notice from its file header, and the Apache-2.0 its package.json names

components.statement: intersection-observer.js says it is licensed under the W3C Software and Document Notice and License (2015 version); its package.json says Apache-2.0. Both texts are included.
components.evidence: The shipped module is intersection-observer.js (sha256 bf73170c8637bae8c328ed21dfb368825343a7abb0abee0498cd04907f7d52ea); its first 8 lines are saved verbatim (with comment markers) as the header text. Neither the npm package nor GoogleChromeLabs/intersection-observer at the npm gitHead a7874945a27061d01e4076b8aae8b30abc756e97 (tree via api.github.com) has a LICENSE file; the file at that commit is byte-identical to the installed one, and the npm tarball (integrity = lockfile) unpacks identical to node_modules. W3C text: SPDX License List v3.29.0 (commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48) text/W3C-20150513.txt, because W3C publishes it only as HTML (https://www.w3.org/Consortium/Legal/2015/copyright-software-and-document, now served at /copyright/software-license-2015/; fetched 2026-10-29, sha256 e3ea81a3892d14b02f3effc82e97674733a9d0e2d410457cc17f0a5a83833461, the page says it was in effect 13 May 2015 to 31 Dec 2022). Compared word by word with that page's licence text: identical except that SPDX writes '(c)' where W3C writes '©' in the change-notice template ('Copyright © [YEAR] W3C®'). Not byte-for-byte from W3C: see REPORT.md. Apache-2.0 text: Indigo's LICENSE at b36d38f5 (= apache.org's LICENSE-2.0.txt).
